title: [NVIDIA] Fix wrong symmetric sizes for fp4 cases (#12640)
body:
## Motivation

The recent [changes](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/7a21d8b2765eabed74d8a8a3abced571b23492d0) seem to have broken the FP4 use cases.
The root cause is that the output shape of MoE should not be assumed to match the input, since FP4 inputs are stored in a packed format while the outputs are typically in higher precision (e.g., BF16).

People might see errors like when using the flashinfer moe backend for nvfp4:
```
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 840, in forward
    combine_input = self.run_moe_core(
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 862, in run_moe_core
    return self.quant_method.apply(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py", line 1607, in apply
    output = flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe(
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py", line 814, in cutlass_fused_moe
    check_shape_dtype_device(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/flashinfer/utils.py", line 526, in check_shape_dtype_device
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: Invalid shape of output: expected (16, 7168), got torch.Size([16, 3584])
```

 
## Modifications

Fixed the issue by using the output dimension from the second weight instead, or doubling the dimension if the input is explicitly FP4.

title: [CPU] Fix TP padding case with weight block size (#8243)
body:
### Motivation
Fixes the [Kimi-K2-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct) (FP8) TP=6 failure on CPU.

ValueError: Weight output_partition_size = 2112 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128.

### Modifications
Considering `weight_block_size `when padding TP, to make self.num_heads * self.qk_head_dim / tp_size divisible by `weight_block_size `in the below ColumnParallelLinear.
```
  self.q_b_proj = ColumnParallelLinear(
      q_lora_rank,
      self.num_heads * self.qk_head_dim,
      bias=False,
      quant_config=quant_config,
      prefix=add_prefix("q_b_proj", prefix),
      tp_rank=attn_tp_rank,
      tp_size=attn_tp_size,
  )
```
In our case, self.num_heads = 64, self.qk_head_dim =192, tp_size = 6, block_size = 128

Before this PR, self.num_heads is padded to 66, self.num_heads * self.qk_head_dim / tp_size = 2112, which is not divisible by 128.
After this PR, self.num_heads is padded to 72, self.num_heads * self.qk_head_dim / tp_size = 2304, which is divisible by 128.



**MISC.**
This PR also covers a minor fix for unquant MoE module with `apply_router_weight_on_input` config, sine CPU AMX path supports now.

title: [Ascend] support Kimi-K2-Thinking (#12759)
body: ## Motivation Kimi-K2-Think model Day 0 support on SGLang on Ascend NPU backend. Ascend has completed the adaptation of the INT4 Weight (A16W4, pergroup=32) quantization format for the K2 Think model, balancing inference speed and precision. Meanwhile, the supporting GMM (GroupedMatmul) kernel has been fully open-sourced, providing a more flexible engineering foundation for low-bit inference of large models. This optimization not only reduces the memory usage of model operation but also lays the groundwork for the efficient deployment of larger-scale models in the future. In practical applications, a single Ascend Atlas 800I A3 device can complete the deployment of the Kimi-K2-Think model, greatly lowering the deployment threshold for a wide range of customers. ## Modifications We support a new class of NPU_W4A16MoEMethod for npu to support A16W4 weights in MOE part. Because the weights is stored with int32 dtype, NPU needs to pack and unpack functions to convert the weights for NPU. ## Accuracy Tests python3 few shot_gsm8k.py --data-path /path/to/test.jsonl.txt --parallel 16 --num-questions 200 --num-shots 5 --port 30002 --temperature tee answer.loq ## Instalation ### 1. start docker ``` docker pull docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:dsv32-a3 ``` ### 2. build form source ``` pip install xgrammar==0.1.26 git clone -b kimi-k2-thinking (PR) https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git cd sglang # install entrypoint for NPU is python/pyproject_other.toml，one needs to replace pyproject.toml with python/pyproject_other.toml.'. mv python/pyproject_toml.toml python/pyproject.toml pip install "python[srt_npu]" ``` ### 3. launch the server ```[shell] export SGLANG_DEEPEP_BF16_DISPATCH=1 export p0='x.x.x.x' python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \ --quantization w8a8_int8 \ --tp 16 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --max-total-tokens 66000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend ascend \ --device npu \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30002 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --context-length 8192 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8000 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --disable-overlap-schedule \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --nnodes $nnodes --node-rank $node_id --dist-init-addr ${p0}:10000 \ --watchdog-timeout 9000 ``` ## Benchmarking and Profiling ## Checklist

body: ## Motivation This PR improves DeepSeek-R1 w4afp8 TP8/EP8 ITL performance. It is motivated by the following profiling trace, obtained by running DeepSeek-R1 w4afp8 TP8 with a concurrency level (i.e., batch size) of 4: The trace reveals several performance gaps: - The grouped GEMM kernel is a major bottleneck. - The pre-reorder, post-reorder, and compute_expert_offsets_w4a8 kernels are inefficient. - There are too many small kernels that should be fused. ## Modifications Note that this PR does not optimize the w4afp8 grouped GEMM kernel.
